transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Lately I can’t think straight at work—decisions that used to be easy now leave me stuck and second-guessing everything. It actually led to a difficult performance check-in recently, and my HR partner suggested I come in for an evaluation.

Did these concentration and self-doubt problems begin after a specific stressful event or change at work or in your life, or have they been building up more generally over time? Have you also been feeling down or losing interest in things most days?

These problems really flared up about three months ago when I took on a high-pressure project at work, though I've noticed milder cycles of highs and lows since my mid-twenties. Along with that, I've felt this heavy, gray film over everything that leaves me hollow and tearful, and I've completely lost my appetite and interest in food.

Do you feel down and uninterested most of the day nearly every day even outside of work, or do these feelings mainly happen when you’re dealing with the stressful project? Have they continued even when the work stress eases?

Yes, this heavy, gray film is constant and affects everything, even when I'm away from work and the stress eases. It has been dragging on for about three months now, making me lose interest in things like eating or going out. I've actually been cycling through these highs and crashes since my mid-twenties, so it's a long-standing pattern rather than just a temporary reaction to this project.

During your “high” periods, have you ever had at least 4 days in a row of clearly increased energy or unusually elevated or irritable mood with less need for sleep, talking more, racing thoughts, or impulsive behavior? If so, did those times cause obvious problems or lead to hospitalization?

Yes, since my mid-twenties I've had stretches lasting weeks where I only needed three or four hours of sleep, talked at "1.5x speed," and took on massive amounts of extra work. I never needed hospitalization during those times because I felt incredibly capable and energized, though coworkers did notice I was buzzing and occasionally irritable. The severe disruption to my life and work only really hit when I crashed into this current low phase.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a long-standing bipolar course with recurrent periods since the mid-twenties of weeks-long elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, increased talkativeness, and overactivity consistent with hypomanic episodes, followed by a current approximately 3-month depressive episode with persistent low mood, tearfulness, indecisiveness/concentration problems, anhedonia, and reduced appetite. There is no evidence of hospitalization or psychotic/manic severity during the highs, supporting bipolar affective disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression.
